title: Prakrama 2, Sarga 17. The Admonition of Sri Murari Gupta
html:
For a week the Lord's wondrous radiance lingers; Srivasa asks about the dharma of the ages, and the Lord speaks of the holy name; the Lord longs to leave for Mathura, and Murari holds Him back

Verse 1

श्रीचन्द्रशेखराचार्यरत्नवाट्यां महाप्रभुः।
ननर्त यत्र तत्रासीत्तेजस्तत्त्ववदद्भुतम्॥१॥

śrīcandraśekharācāryaratnavāṭyāṁ mahāprabhuḥ|
nanarta yatra tatrāsīttejastattvavadadbhutam||1||

shri-chandrashekhara-acharyaratna-vatyam — in the homestead of Sri Chandrashekhara Acharyaratna; maha-prabhuh — Mahaprabhu; nanarta — danced; yatra — where; tatra — there; asit — there was; tejah — a radiance; tattva-vat — in very truth; adbhutam — wondrous.

1In the homestead of Sri Chandrashekhara Acharyaratna1, where Mahaprabhu had danced, a radiance shone forth — wondrous in very truth.

Verse 2

सप्ताहं शीतलं चन्द्रतेजसा सदृशं हरेः।
चञ्चलेव सुदुष्प्रेक्ष्यं चित्ताह्लादकरं शुचि॥२॥

saptāhaṁ śītalaṁ candratejasā sadṛśaṁ hareḥ|
cañcaleva suduṣprekṣyaṁ cittāhlādakaraṁ śuci||2||

sapta-aham — for seven days; shitalam — cool; chandra-tejasa — to the light of the moon; sadrisham — similar; hareh — of Hari; chanchala — lightning; iva — like; su-dushprekshyam — very hard to look at; chitta-ahlada-karam — gladdening the heart; shuchi — pure.

2For seven days Hari's radiance was cool like moonlight, yet dazzling to the eyes like lightning — pure and gladdening to the heart.

Verse 3

ये ये तत्रागता लोका ऊचुस्तत्र कथं दृशोः।
उन्मीलने न शक्ताः स्म विद्युद्वत्प्रेक्ष्य भूतले॥३॥

ye ye tatrāgatā lokā ūcustatra kathaṁ dṛśoḥ|
unmīlane na śaktāḥ sma vidyudvatprekṣya bhūtale||3||

ye ye — all who; tatra — there; agatah — came; lokah — people; uchuh — said; tatra — there; katham — how is it; drishoh — of the eyes; unmilane — to the opening; na shaktah sma — we are not able; vidyut-vat — something like lightning; prekshya — seeing; bhu-tale — on the earth.

3All who came there said, "How is it that we cannot open our eyes? It is as if we were seeing lightning on the earth!"

Verse 4

तच्छ्रुत्वा वैष्णवाः सर्वे हर्षादूचुर्न किञ्चन।
जानन्तोऽपि महाभागा बहिर्मुखजनान्प्रति॥४॥

tacchrutvā vaiṣṇavāḥ sarve harṣādūcurna kiñcana|
jānanto'pi mahābhāgā bahirmukhajanānprati||4||

tat — that; shrutva — hearing; vaishnavah — the Vaishnavas; sarve — all; harshat — out of joy; uchuh na kinchana — said nothing; janantah — knowing; api — though; maha-bhagah — the greatly fortunate; bahir-mukha-janan prati — to the people turned away (from God).

4Hearing this, the Vaishnavas, out of joy, said nothing: those greatly fortunate souls knew the truth of it, but did not reveal it to people turned away from God.

Verse 5

अथ पप्रच्छ श्रीवासो भगवन्तं जगद्गुरुम्।
कलावेव हरेर्नामकीर्तनं समुदाहृतम्॥५॥

atha papraccha śrīvāso bhagavantaṁ jagadgurum|
kalāveva harernāmakīrtanaṁ samudāhṛtam||5||

atha — then; paprachchha — asked; shrivasah — Srivasa; bhagavantam — Bhagavan; jagat-gurum — the teacher of the world; kalau eva — for Kali alone; hareh — of Hari; nama-kirtanam — the chanting of the name; samudahritam — is declared.

5Then Srivasa asked Bhagavan, the teacher of the world, "The chanting of Hari's name is declared for the age of Kali alone.

Verse 6

किं सत्यादियुगस्यास्ति फलं न्यूनं कथञ्चन।
तच्छ्रुत्वा भगवान्प्राह श्रूयतां कथयामि ते॥६॥

kiṁ satyādiyugasyāsti phalaṁ nyūnaṁ kathañcana|
tacchrutvā bhagavānprāha śrūyatāṁ kathayāmi te||6||

kim — is it that; satya-adi-yugasya — of Satya and the other ages; asti — is; phalam — the fruit; nyunam — lesser; kathanchana — in any way; tat — that; shrutva — hearing; bhagavan — Bhagavan; praha — said; shruyatam — listen; kathayami — I shall tell; te — you.

6Is the fruit of the Satya age and the others, then, in any way less?2" Hearing this, Bhagavan replied, "Listen, and I shall tell you.

Verse 7

सत्ये धर्मस्य पूर्णत्वाद्ध्यानेनैवोपसाध्यते।
तत्फलं यज्ञमात्रेण त्रेतायां द्वापरे युगे॥७॥

satye dharmasya pūrṇatvāddhyānenaivopasādhyate|
tatphalaṁ yajñamātreṇa tretāyāṁ dvāpare yuge||7||

satye — in the Satya age; dharmasya — of dharma; purnatvat — because of the fullness; dhyanena eva — by meditation alone; upasadhyate — is attained; tat-phalam — that fruit; yajna-matrena — by sacrifice alone; tretayam — in the Treta age; dvapare yuge — in the Dvapara age.

7In the Satya age, when dharma is whole, the fruit is attained by meditation alone; in the Treta age the same fruit comes by sacrifice alone; in the Dvapara age,

Verse 8

पूजनेन कलौ पापैर्न शक्तास्ते हरिः स्वयम्।
नामस्वरूपो भगवानागत्य शुशुभे प्रभुः॥८॥

pūjanena kalau pāpairna śaktāste hariḥ svayam|
nāmasvarūpo bhagavānāgatya śuśubhe prabhuḥ||8||

pujanena — by worship (in Dvapara); kalau — in Kali; papaih — because of sins; na shaktah — not capable; te — they (people); harih — Hari; svayam — Himself; nama-svarupah — in the form of the name; bhagavan — Bhagavan; agatya — having come; shushubhe — shone forth; prabhuh — the Lord.

8by worship. But in Kali people, because of their sins, are capable of none of these; and so Hari Himself, Bhagavan, the Lord, has come in the form of the name and shone forth3.

Verse 9

कृतादिषु त्रयः शक्त्या ध्यानयज्ञार्चनादयः।
दारुणे च कलौ पापे स्वयमेवानुपद्यते॥९॥

kṛtādiṣu trayaḥ śaktyā dhyānayajñārcanādayaḥ|
dāruṇe ca kalau pāpe svayamevānupadyate||9||

krita-adishu — in Krita and the other (ages); trayah — the three (ways); shaktya — by (human) capacity; dhyana-yajna-archana-adayah — meditation, sacrifice, worship and the rest; darune — in the terrible; cha — but; kalau — Kali; pape — sinful; svayam eva — He Himself; anupadyate — comes.

9In Krita and the ages that follow, the three ways — meditation, sacrifice, worship and the rest — are carried out by human strength; but in the terrible, sinful age of Kali He comes Himself."

Verse 10

तच्छ्रुत्वा हर्षितो विप्रः श्रीवासः पण्डितोत्तमः।
मेने सर्वपुरुषार्थसारं श्रीनाममङ्गलम्॥१०॥

tacchrutvā harṣito vipraḥ śrīvāsaḥ paṇḍitottamaḥ|
mene sarvapuruṣārthasāraṁ śrīnāmamaṅgalam||10||

tat — that; shrutva — hearing; harshitah — delighted; viprah — the brahmana; shrivasah — Srivasa; pandita-uttamah — the best of pandits; mene — considered; sarva-purusha-artha-saram — the essence of all human goals; shri-nama-mangalam — the auspicious holy name.

10Hearing this, the brahmana Srivasa, the best of pandits, rejoiced and recognized the auspicious holy name as the essence of all the aims of human life.

Verse 11

हरिसङ्कीर्तनं कृत्वा नगरे नगरे प्रभुः।
म्लेच्छादीनुद्दधारासौ जगतामीश्वरो हरिः॥११॥

harisaṅkīrtanaṁ kṛtvā nagare nagare prabhuḥ|
mlecchādīnuddadhārāsau jagatāmīśvaro hariḥ||11||

hari-sankirtanam — the sankirtana of Hari; kritva — performing; nagare nagare — in town after town; prabhuh — the Lord; mlechchha-adin — the mlechchhas and others; uddadhara — delivered; asau — He; jagatam — of the worlds; ishvarah — the Sovereign; harih — Hari.

11Thus, performing the sankirtana of Hari in town after town, the Lord — Hari, the Sovereign of the worlds — delivered the mlechchhas and others.

Verse 12

एकदा भगवानाह नेत्रवारिभराप्लुतः।
स्थातुं नाहं समर्थोऽस्मि गच्छामि मथुरां पुरीम्॥१२॥

ekadā bhagavānāha netravāribharāplutaḥ|
sthātuṁ nāhaṁ samartho'smi gacchāmi mathurāṁ purīm||12||

ekada — once; bhagavan — Bhagavan; aha — said; netra-vari-bhara-aplutah — flooded with a stream of tears; sthatum — to stay; na — not; aham — I; samarthah asmi — am able; gachchhami — I am going; mathuram — to Mathura; purim — the city.

12One day Bhagavan, bathed in tears, said, "I can no longer stay here. I am going to the city of Mathura."

Verse 13

छित्त्वा यज्ञोपवीतं स्वं कृष्णविश्लेषकातरः।
श्रुत्वा तद्वचनं तस्य प्राह वैद्यो मुरारिकः॥१३॥

chittvā yajñopavītaṁ svaṁ kṛṣṇaviśleṣakātaraḥ|
śrutvā tadvacanaṁ tasya prāha vaidyo murārikaḥ||13||

chhittva — breaking; yajna-upavitam — the sacred thread; svam — His own; krishna-vishlesha-katarah — distraught at separation from Krishna; shrutva — hearing; tat — those; vachanam — words; tasya — His; praha — said; vaidyah — the physician; murarikah — (humble) Murari.

13In the anguish of separation from Krishna He broke His sacred thread4. Hearing His words, the humble physician Murari said:

Verse 14

भगवन्सकलं कर्तुं शक्तोऽसि सर्वतत्त्ववित्।
गन्तुं स्थातुं त्वमार्येण तथापि नार्हसि ध्रुवम्॥१४॥

bhagavansakalaṁ kartuṁ śakto'si sarvatattvavit|
gantuṁ sthātuṁ tvamāryeṇa tathāpi nārhasi dhruvam||14||

bhagavan — O Bhagavan; sakalam — everything; kartum — to do; shaktah asi — You are able; sarva-tattva-vit — knower of all truths; gantum — to go; sthatum — to stay; tvam — You; aryena — by (the way of) the noble; tatha api — even so; na arhasi — You ought not; dhruvam — surely.

14"Bhagavan, You can do anything, You know all truths; You are free to go or to stay. Even so, by the way of the noble5, You surely ought not to go.

Verse 15

त्वया चेत्क्रियते नाथ स्वातन्त्र्यात्सकला जनाः।
स्वातन्त्र्येण करिष्यन्ति पतिष्यन्त्यशुचौ पुनः॥१५॥

tvayā cetkriyate nātha svātantryātsakalā janāḥ|
svātantryeṇa kariṣyanti patiṣyantyaśucau punaḥ||15||

tvaya — by You; chet — if; kriyate — it is done; natha — O Lord; svatantryat — out of independence; sakalah — all; janah — people; svatantryena — independently; karishyanti — will act; patishyanti — will fall; ashuchau — into impurity; punah — then.

15If You, O Lord, act as You alone will, then all people too will act as they will — and fall into impurity.

Verse 16

एतन्मत्वा स्वयं तात स्वाश्रमादाश्रमान्तरम्।
कर्तव्यं तु त्वया ते के कथयन्तु महत्तमाः॥१६॥

etanmatvā svayaṁ tāta svāśramādāśramāntaram|
kartavyaṁ tu tvayā te ke kathayantu mahattamāḥ||16||

etat — this; matva — considering; svayam — Yourself; tata — dear one; sva-ashramat — from Your own ashrama; ashrama-antaram — (a change) to another ashrama; kartavyam — is to be made; tu — but; tvaya — by You; te ke — who are they; kathayantu — let them say; mahattamah — the greatest.

16Consider this, dear one: that You Yourself should pass from Your own ashrama into another — which of the greatest would say it must be so?

Verse 17

कृत्वैव गमनं तेऽद्य कृतं स्यात्सर्वदेहिनाम्।
चैतन्यरहितानां च किं तावत्कथयामि ते॥१७॥

kṛtvaiva gamanaṁ te'dya kṛtaṁ syātsarvadehinām|
caitanyarahitānāṁ ca kiṁ tāvatkathayāmi te||17||

kritva eva — once making; gamanam — departure; te — Your; adya — today; kritam syat — it would be all over; sarva-dehinam — for all embodied beings; chaitanya-rahitanam — bereft of consciousness (of Chaitanya); cha — and; kim — what; tavat — more; kathayami — shall I say; te — to You.

17Should You leave today, it will be the end of all embodied beings: they will be left without Chaitanya, without consciousness6. What more can I say to You?"

Verse 18

भक्तैः संवेष्टितो नित्यं नित्यानन्दसमन्वितः।
गदाधरेण गन्धाद्यैः सेवितो भक्तगो हरिः॥१८॥

bhaktaiḥ saṁveṣṭito nityaṁ nityānandasamanvitaḥ|
gadādhareṇa gandhādyaiḥ sevito bhaktago hariḥ||18||

bhaktaih — by devotees; samveshtitah — surrounded; nityam — always; nityananda-samanvitah — accompanied by Nityananda; gadadharena — by Gadadhara; gandha-adyaih — with fragrances and so on; sevitah — served; bhakta-gah — abiding among His devotees; harih — Hari.

18Hari was ever surrounded by His devotees, Nityananda was with Him, and Gadadhara served Him with fragrances and other offerings — for He dwells among His devotees7.

Verse 19

तच्छ्रुत्वा भगवांस्तूष्णीं भूत्वासीत्प्रेमविह्वलः।
कृष्णसङ्कीर्तनानन्दपूर्णमनोरथः स्वयम्॥१९॥

tacchrutvā bhagavāṁstūṣṇīṁ bhūtvāsītpremavihvalaḥ|
kṛṣṇasaṅkīrtanānandapūrṇamanorathaḥ svayam||19||

tat — that; shrutva — hearing; bhagavan — Bhagavan; tushnim bhutva — falling silent; asit — remained; prema-vihvalah — overwhelmed by love; krishna-sankirtana-ananda-purna-manorathah — His desires fulfilled by the bliss of Krishna's sankirtana; svayam — Himself.

19Hearing Murari's words, Bhagavan fell silent, overwhelmed by love; all His desires were fulfilled in the bliss of Krishna's sankirtana.

Thus ends the seventeenth sarga, "The Admonition of Sri Murari Gupta" (Sri-murari-gupta-anushasana), of the second prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. Chandrashekhara Acharyaratna was the Lord's maternal uncle; the play described in sargas 2.15–16 was staged in his house.
  2. Srivasa asks: if the chanting of the name is declared specifically for the Kali age, are the ways of the other ages not inferior to it? The Lord's answer (vv. 7–9) shows that in every age the same fruit is attained, but in Kali the Lord comes Himself — as the holy name.
  3. The name of Hari is not different from Hari Himself.
  4. The sacred thread is the mark of the twice-born householder; by breaking it the Lord foreshadows His leaving home and accepting sannyasa.
  5. The reading and sense of this passage are not entirely clear.
  6. A play on words: "bereft of consciousness" in Sanskrit is "bereft of chaitanya."
  7. Literally "going with the devotees" (bhakta-ga).
